name: Cybench
intro: Cybench是一个用于评估语言模型在网络安全任务中能力和风险的框架。它包含40个专业级别的夺旗（CTF）任务，这些任务来源于4个不同的CTF竞赛，涵盖了广泛的难度。每个任务都包含描述、起始文件，并在一个代理可以执行命令和观察输出的环境中初始化。为了更详细的评估，每个任务还引入了子任务。
build_method: 从四个 2022–2024 年专业 CTF 竞赛筛选 40 题，覆盖六类技能和 2 分钟至 24 小时 54 分钟首解时间；为每题补充子任务、标准解脚本、CI 与服务存活检查
metric: 无引导成功率、子任务引导最终成功率、宏平均子任务完成率、最难已解题首解时间，以及 Token/耗时
build_method_en: Select 40 tasks from four professional 2022–2024 CTFs across six categories and first-solve times from 2 minutes to 24 h 54 min; add subtasks, a solution script, CI, and server liveness checks
intro_en: Cybench is a framework for evaluating language models' capabilities and risks in cybersecurity tasks. It includes 40 professional-level CTF tasks sourced from 4 different CTF competitions, covering a wide range of difficulties. Each task contains a description, starter files, and is initialized in an environment where an agent can execute commands and observe outputs. For more detailed evaluation, each task also includes subtasks.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2408.08926 Sections 2–4, the official Cybench website, and andyzorigin/cybench repository. Cybench selects 40 recent professional-level tasks from HackTheBox Cyber Apocalypse 2024, SekaiCTF 2022–23, GlacierCTF and HKCert CTF. The 2022–2024 timing mitigates train-test overlap; tasks proxy real cybersecurity skills across cryptography, web, reverse engineering, forensics, exploitation and miscellaneous categories. Human first-solve time grounds difficulty from 2 minutes to 24 hours 54 minutes. Every task contains a description, starter files and evaluator, runs in a common Kali Linux environment with local files and isolated remote task servers, and receives sequential intermediate question/answer subtasks. A ground-truth solution script must reproduce the exact flag; CI confirms the task is buildable and solvable and automated probes confirm servers are alive. The agent repeats an action–execution–observation–memory loop with Bash commands. Unguided mode has one objective and binary success; subtask mode retains memory across sequential checkpoints and reports both final-task binary success and fractional subtask completion. The evaluator compares submitted answers to the key. Reports include unguided success, subtask-guided success, macro-averaged subtask percentage, hardest solved task by human first-solve time, token use and elapsed time.
